findings.detail:
# mobile composer

owner: `mobile/example-app`

a mobile-only refinement of the
[portable composer contract](../../../../../../packages/conversation-contract/docs/development/specifications/composer/index.md).

- [product specification](product-spec.md)
- [requirements](requirements.md)
# product specification

the portable
[composer contract](../../../../../../packages/conversation-contract/docs/development/specifications/composer/product-spec.md)
covers message validity and submission for all clients: clients submit
non-empty text messages through a composer. this specification refines that
contract for the mobile app only and does not change portable behavior.

mobile adds composer behavior the portable contract deliberately leaves out
(platform layout and interaction):

- **multiline input.** the composer accepts multiline text. the input area
  grows with its content while staying within a bounded composer height.
  submission happens through the send control, not the return key.
- **keyboard avoidance.** when the on-screen keyboard appears, the composer
  stays visible above it, keeping the composed text readable while typing.
- **send-button placement.** the send control is part of the composer and sits
  at its trailing edge, beside the text input.
- **accessibility labels.** the text input and the send control expose
  accessibility labels that identify the message entry field and the send
  action.

the composer is not implemented yet. current status is tracked in
[requirements](requirements.md).
# requirements

| id | requirement | implementation | verification | documentation | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| mobile-composer-001 | the composer accepts multiline text, and the input area grows with its content within a bounded composer height. | not implemented | unverified | pending | — |
| mobile-composer-002 | the composer stays visible above the on-screen keyboard while text entry is active. | not implemented | unverified | pending | — |
| mobile-composer-003 | the send control is part of the composer and sits at its trailing edge, beside the text input. | not implemented | unverified | pending | — |
| mobile-composer-004 | the text input and send control expose accessibility labels identifying the message entry field and the send action. | not implemented | unverified | pending | — |

**`packages/conversation-contract/docs/development/specifications/composer/product-spec.md`**

producers.prompt: Please complete the useful, portable first version approved in `tasks/batch-offline-sync.md`. Keep the package development index, specification, requirements, and decisions consistent. Do not implement the protocol.
producers.response:
All approved work is complete. No protocol code was written; `src/batch.py` is unchanged.

## What was created/changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/batch-sdk/docs/development/specifications/offline-sync/index.md` | New — the package-owned offline synchronization specification |
| `.../offline-sync/requirements.md` | New — stable requirements `BOS-001`–`BOS-007` with separate states |
| `.../offline-sync/decisions.md` | New — single decisions file, as the task directs (no `decisions/` directory) |
| `packages/batch-sdk/docs/development/index.md` | Updated — replaces "No offline synchronization specification exists" with links to the spec, requirements, and decisions, plus a current-behavior note |

## How the checklist is covered

- **Substantial package-owned specification** — placed at `packages/batch-sdk/docs/development/specifications/offline-sync/` per the Crystal Lattice convention for package-owned capability specifications. It defines the offline model (deferral → durable queue → recovery → resubmission), conflict resolution, persisted-queue migration, compatibility, recovery boundaries, and ordering.
- **Required topics** — conflict resolution (acknowledgment-based, deterministic, enqueue-order tiebreaker), queue migration (persistence-contract encoding, versioned records, un-migratable records preserved and surfaced), compatibility (contract refinement-only rule plus an upgrade promise that queued batches survive compatible upgrades), and recovery (bounded by the persistence contract, observable outcome, no discarding on failed recovery).
- **Contracts linked, not copied** — the transport and persistence contract pages are referenced by relative link (verified resolving); the spec constrains itself to "refinement only, never weakening" instead of restating their content.
- **Stable requirements, target-only** — all seven requirements carry stable `BOS-` IDs and begin at implementation *Not started*, verification *Unverified*, documentation *Pending*, per the repository's state vocabulary; the specification carries a short implementation note stating the protocol is a target that is **not implemented and unverified**, so readers can't mistake the target for available behavior.
- **Decisions** — five material choices with their rejected alternatives recorded in one `decisions.md`: package ownership, reuse of the persistence-contract encoding/migration, acknowledgment-based conflict resolution, allowing reordering after restart, and preserving un-migratable records. The single-file choice itself is recorded there with its rationale.

README was left unchanged — its "submits online batches" claim remains accurate for current behavior, and presenting the offline target as available in user-facing docs is prohibited before implementation. Relative links in all four touched files were verified to resolve; the index no longer contradicts the specification.

findings.detail:
# portable composer contract

owner: `packages/conversation-contract`

- [product specification](product-spec.md)
- [requirements](requirements.md)

# product specification

all clients submit non-empty text messages through a composer. portable
behavior covers message validity, submission, and the composer interaction
behaviors below; visual styling remains a platform concern.

every client provides:

- a composer that accepts multiline text entry;
- a send control presented with the composer, adjacent to its text entry;
- composer and send-control visibility and usability while the platform
  presents an on-screen keyboard (keyboard avoidance);
- accessibility labels for the text entry and the send control.

not implemented: only non-empty-text submission exists today
(composer-001). the behaviors above are the specified target; their current
state is tracked in [requirements](requirements.md).
# requirements

| id | requirement | implementation | verification | documentation | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| composer-001 | clients submit non-empty text. | implemented | automated | documented | existing clients |

# mobile composer refinement

owner: `mobile/example-app`

this specification refines the [portable composer
contract](../../../../../../packages/conversation-contract/docs/development/specifications/composer/index.md)
for the mobile example app. the portable contract remains authoritative for
message validity and submission; this specification covers mobile layout and
accessibility behavior.

- [product specification](product-spec.md)
- [requirements](requirements.md)
# product specification

the mobile composer accepts multiline input while preserving the portable
composer contract for submitting non-empty text messages.

when the software keyboard is visible, keyboard avoidance keeps the composer
and its send control visible and usable above the keyboard. the send control
is placed at the trailing edge of the composer row, adjacent to the multiline
input.

the multiline input has the accessibility label `message`. the send control
has the accessibility label `send message`. these labels identify the text
entry and submission actions to assistive-technology users.
# requirements

| mobile-composer-001 | the composer accepts multiline text and submits non-empty messages through the [portable composer contract](../../../../../../packages/conversation-contract/docs/development/specifications/composer/index.md). | not started | unverified | documented | [product specification](product-spec.md) |
| mobile-composer-002 | when the software keyboard is visible, keyboard avoidance keeps the composer and send control visible and usable above it. | not started | unverified | documented | [product specification](product-spec.md) |

# sync-engine

`sync-engine` captures local changes and queues uploads with caller-supplied
idempotency keys.

```python
from sync import capture_local, queue_upload

captured = capture_local("change-1")
queued = queue_upload(captured, "upload-change-1")
```

`queue_upload` preserves the supplied key so a retry can identify the same
upload. empty idempotency keys are rejected with `valueerror`. conflict
resolution for concurrent remote changes is not implemented yet.

# Offline synchronization decisions

These decisions describe the target recorded by the
[offline batch synchronization specification](index.md). They do not
authorize or constitute a protocol implementation.

## Package-specific lifecycle with shared contract authority

The batch SDK owns the lifecycle that connects a batch submission to durable
queueing and replay. Delivery semantics remain governed by the
[transport contract](../../../../../transport-contract/docs/development/specifications/transport/index.md),
and durable encoding, migration, and recovery boundaries remain governed by
the [persistence contract](../../../../../persistence-contract/docs/development/specifications/persistence/index.md).

This boundary keeps batch-specific conflict and recovery behavior close to
the batch package while avoiding a second definition of shared transport or
persistence semantics.

## Durable acceptance is the handoff boundary

A submission is accepted for later synchronization only after its complete
replayable record is durable. This makes the acceptance claim meaningful
across process interruption: work before the boundary may be unaccepted, and
work after the boundary remains recoverable.

The boundary applies whether the first attempt is made immediately or after
an offline period. It does not require the SDK to claim delivery before the
transport has acknowledged it.

## Logical identity governs duplicates and conflicts

The logical submission identity is stable across retries, restarts, and
supported migrations. Equivalent payloads with that identity are coalesced or
treated as already delivered; a different payload with the same identity is
retained as an explicit conflict.

The SDK does not silently choose one conflicting payload or invent a server
merge policy. This preserves evidence for explicit resolution and prevents a
local replay decision from changing the meaning of an existing submission.

## Migration preserves meaning, and recovery preserves uncertainty

Queue records are versioned and migrated through the persistence contract.
Migration may change representation, but not logical identity, payload
meaning, or delivery state. Unknown, corrupt, or interrupted records remain
unresolved within the persistence recovery boundary instead of being
discarded or reintroduced as new submissions.

Acknowledgement is recorded before cleanup. A restart may reconsider an
in-flight record, but transport idempotency makes that reconsideration safe;
it does not replay a durably acknowledged record as new work.
# Offline batch synchronization

Status: Target behavior; not implemented

This specification defines how the batch SDK accepts work when delivery is
temporarily unavailable and later synchronizes that work through the shared
transport and persistence contracts. It is package-specific: it describes the
batch lifecycle and the relationship between those contracts without
redefining either contract.

The target is not part of the current SDK behavior. The current
`submit_batch` implementation returns a local item count and does not yet
deliver, persist, replay, or recover batches.

## Contract boundaries

The [transport contract](../../../../../transport-contract/docs/development/specifications/transport/index.md)
remains authoritative for request delivery, retryable transport errors, and
idempotency keys. This specification determines when a batch is eligible for
delivery and how a queued batch is replayed; it does not define another retry
taxonomy or idempotency-key contract.

The [persistence contract](../../../../../persistence-contract/docs/development/specifications/persistence/index.md)
remains authoritative for durable record encoding, schema migration, and
recovery boundaries. This specification determines what the batch queue must
preserve across those operations; it does not duplicate their storage
mechanics.

## Submission and delivery

A batch submission has one logical identity that remains stable across process
restarts, transport retries, and queue migration. The identity is used with
the transport contract so that replay cannot turn one accepted logical batch
into multiple successful deliveries.

The SDK may deliver a submission immediately when the transport is available.
When delivery is temporarily unavailable, it must durably record the complete
submission before reporting that the work has been accepted for later
synchronization. A process interruption before that durable boundary leaves
the submission unaccepted; an interruption after it leaves a recoverable queue
record.

Successful delivery is recorded before the queue record is removed or
compacted. Replaying a record whose acknowledgement was not durably recorded
must remain safe under the transport contract's idempotency behavior.
Automatic removal must not be the only evidence that delivery succeeded.

The queue is a delivery aid, not a second source of truth for the batch
payload. A queued record retains the payload needed for replay and the
identity and state needed to distinguish pending, in-flight, acknowledged,
and terminally unresolved work. Transport-defined retryability determines
whether an unsuccessful attempt is eligible for replay; the SDK must not
silently discard an unresolved record.

## Conflict resolution

Two submissions with the same logical identity and equivalent payload are one
logical submission. The queue must coalesce them or otherwise ensure that
replay produces one transport identity rather than duplicate work.

The same logical identity paired with a different payload is a conflict. The
SDK must not silently replace the durable payload or merge the two payloads.
It preserves the existing record and records the conflicting submission as
unresolved for explicit handling. A conflict is not treated as a successful
delivery.

An acknowledgement for the logical identity is authoritative for later
replay. Once acknowledged, a duplicate equivalent submission may be treated
as already delivered; a conflicting submission remains a conflict rather than
being rewritten as an update.

## Persisted queue migration

Every persisted queue record has a schema version and enough identity
metadata to select the correct migration. A reader migrates a supported older
record to the current representation before delivery scheduling uses it.
Migration preserves the logical identity, payload, delivery state, and
information needed to apply the transport contract.

Migration must not silently reinterpret an unknown or corrupt record as a new
submission. Records that cannot be recovered within the persistence
contract's recovery boundary remain unresolved and retain enough diagnostic
context for an explicit recovery action. A migration interruption must leave
either the prior valid record or the fully migrated record available for
recovery.

## Compatibility

The logical identity and payload semantics remain stable across SDK upgrades
that retain the queue schema. A newer SDK may add representation details
through the persistence contract's migration mechanism, but it must not change
an existing record's identity or payload meaning as an incidental migration
effect.

The package follows the transport contract for retry classification,
idempotency, and delivery outcomes, and follows the persistence contract for
encoding, migration, and recovery. A change to either shared contract can
therefore affect synchronization compatibility and must be evaluated at this
boundary.

The current count-only return value is not evidence that a batch was
delivered or durably queued. Until implementation exists, callers must not
interpret the target acceptance and synchronization behavior as available.

## Recovery

Recovery scans durable queue records after startup or another persistence
recovery boundary and resumes only records that are still eligible for
delivery. In-flight records are safe to reconsider because their logical
identity is stable and transport idempotency governs duplicate attempts.

Acknowledged records are not replayed as new work. Records with terminally
unresolved transport or persistence outcomes remain visible to recovery
handling and are not converted to success by a restart. Recovery must
preserve the distinction between accepted work awaiting delivery, work
whose delivery is acknowledged, and work requiring explicit resolution.

## Non-goals for this target

This specification does not define a new transport protocol, a replacement
persistence engine, a server-side merge policy, or an implementation of the
batch queue. Those concerns remain outside the package target described here
or are governed by the linked contracts.
# Offline synchronization requirements

All requirements in this record begin as not implemented and unverified.
Stage A documents the target and its decisions; it does not implement the
protocol. Documentation is marked complete because the target is recorded
here.

| ID | Requirement | Implementation | Verification | Documentation | Primary evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BATCH-OFFLINE-001 | A submission that cannot be delivered temporarily is durably recorded before the SDK reports it accepted for later synchronization. | Not started | Unverified | Documented | [Submission and delivery](index.md#submission-and-delivery) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-002 | One logical submission keeps a stable identity across retries, restarts, and supported queue migrations. | Not started | Unverified | Documented | [Submission and delivery](index.md#submission-and-delivery) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-003 | Equivalent submissions with the same logical identity do not produce duplicate successful delivery, while a same-identity payload conflict is preserved and not silently overwritten. | Not started | Unverified | Documented | [Conflict resolution](index.md#conflict-resolution) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-004 | Replay uses the transport contract's retryability, idempotency, and delivery outcomes without defining a competing transport policy. | Not started | Unverified | Documented | [Contract boundaries](index.md#contract-boundaries) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-005 | Persisted queue records are versioned and supported older records can be migrated without changing their identity, payload meaning, or delivery state. | Not started | Unverified | Documented | [Persisted queue migration](index.md#persisted-queue-migration) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-006 | Unknown, corrupt, or interrupted queue migrations remain recoverable within the persistence contract's recovery boundary and are not silently treated as new submissions. | Not started | Unverified | Documented | [Persisted queue migration](index.md#persisted-queue-migration) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-007 | SDK upgrades that retain the queue schema preserve the meaning of existing logical identities and payloads, while changes to the shared transport or persistence contracts are treated as synchronization compatibility changes. | Not started | Unverified | Documented | [Compatibility](index.md#compatibility) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-008 | Recovery distinguishes queued work, acknowledged work, and unresolved work; restart does not replay acknowledged work as new work or turn unresolved work into success. | Not started | Unverified | Documented | [Recovery](index.md#recovery) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-009 | Successful delivery is durably recorded before a queue record is removed or compacted, so removal alone is not the only evidence of acknowledgement. | Not started | Unverified | Documented | [Submission and delivery](index.md#submission-and-delivery) |

## Shared contract references

- [Transport contract](../../../../../transport-contract/docs/development/specifications/transport/index.md)
  defines request delivery, retryable transport errors, and idempotency keys.
- [Persistence contract](../../../../../persistence-contract/docs/development/specifications/persistence/index.md)
  defines durable record encoding, schema migration, and recovery boundaries.
- [Offline batch synchronization specification](index.md) defines the
  package-specific behavior that composes those contracts.
# Batch SDK development

The package documentation describes online batch submission, while the
current implementation only returns a local item count. Offline
synchronization is a target and is not implemented.

## Specifications

- [Offline batch synchronization](specifications/offline-synchronization/index.md)
  defines durable acceptance, replay, conflict resolution, persisted queue
  migration, compatibility, and recovery.
- [Offline synchronization requirements](specifications/offline-synchronization/requirements.md)
  records stable outcomes and their implementation, verification, and
  documentation state.
- [Offline synchronization decisions](specifications/offline-synchronization/decisions.md)
  records the material choices that constrain the target behavior.

```python
publish({"type": "created"})
# {"status": "published", "event": {"type": "created"}}
```

The current retry support is exposed through `retry_state(attempt,
max_attempts=3)`. It returns `"retrying"` while the attempt is below the
configured limit and `"failed"` when the attempt reaches or exceeds that
limit:

```python
retry_state(1)       # "retrying"
retry_state(3)       # "failed"
retry_state(3, 5)    # "retrying"
retry_state(5, 5)    # "failed"
```

`publish()` currently reports a published event; it does not perform delivery
attempts or invoke the retry-state calculation itself.

# Offline synchronization decisions

Material decisions made while writing the offline synchronization
specification (`specifications/offline-sync/index.md`), each against a
credible alternative.

## Package ownership

The offline synchronization specification is owned by `batch-sdk` under
`docs/development/specifications/offline-sync/`. Alternative: a shared
specification beside the transport and persistence contracts. Rejected
because the queue, flush, and retention behavior is `batch-sdk` behavior; the
contracts it builds on remain separately owned and are linked, not absorbed.

## At-least-once delivery with idempotency-key deduplication

Delivery semantics are at-least-once: redelivery after an uncertain failure
is expected, and duplicates are resolved by the transport contract's
idempotency keys. Alternative: at-most-once delivery that drops a batch whose
delivery outcome is unknown. Rejected because losing an accepted batch on a
crash contradicts the goal of offline synchronization; duplicate delivery is
the safer failure, and idempotency keys make it detectable.

## No content-level conflict merging

Conflict resolution is limited to duplicate delivery, resolved by
idempotency keys. Batches are independent and carry no mergeable content, so
no merge or last-writer-wins comparison between batches is defined.
Alternative: content-based conflict resolution. Rejected because the SDK does
not interpret batch content, and any merge rule would be invented semantics
for data only the caller understands.

## Queue state uses the persistence contract, not a local format

Pending batches are encoded with the persistence contract's durable record
encoding and migrated by its schema migration mechanism. Alternative: a
`batch-sdk`-local queue file format with its own migration. Rejected because
it would duplicate contract-owned mechanisms and create a second
compatibility surface to keep aligned.

## Recovery defers to the persistence contract

Recovery happens only within the persistence contract's recovery boundaries;
`batch-sdk` defines what recovered records mean (in flight reverts to
pending, order and keys unchanged) but no recovery mechanism of its own.
Alternative: a `batch-sdk` recovery pass over raw storage. Rejected for the
same duplication reason, and because a second recovery implementation would
risk diverging from the contract's guarantees.

## Failed (non-retryable) batches are retained, not deleted

Batches whose delivery fails without a retryable transport error stay in the
queue as failed pending batches for caller inspection. Alternative: discard
them, or move them to a separate dead-letter store. Rejected because
discarding loses caller data without consent, and a dead-letter store would
add a second persisted state area without a demonstrated need; retention in
place with an explicit state keeps the queue the only local state.

## One decisions file, no decisions directory

All decisions for this specification live in this single `decisions.md` file,
per the Stage A task, rather than a `decisions/` directory of per-decision
records. The decisions here are few enough that one file is easier to read in
full.
# Offline synchronization

Status: Target specification. Not implemented.

`batch-sdk` currently submits batches only while the caller is online: the
existing `submit_batch` entry point performs no delivery of its own and no
persistence. This specification defines the intended offline synchronization
behavior: when delivery is not possible, submitted batches are held in a
durable local queue and delivered later without losing or duplicating them.

The implementation state of individual outcomes is tracked in
[requirements.md](requirements.md). Nothing in this specification describes
available behavior.

## Definitions

- **Batch**: the unit of submission supplied by the caller to the batch
  submission entry point. Batches are independent; no ordering relationship
  exists between separate batches.
- **Pending batch**: a batch that has been accepted for submission but not yet
  acknowledged as delivered through the transport contract.
- **Queue record**: the durable encoding of a pending batch, written with the
  [persistence contract](../../../../../../packages/persistence-contract/docs/development/specifications/persistence/index.md).
- **Flush**: delivery of pending batches to the transport contract.

## Behavior

### Submission while online and offline

Submission takes a batch and returns an accepted result regardless of current
connectivity. When the transport contract reports a retryable transport error,
or when the transport is unavailable, the batch is stored as a pending batch
and the result reports that delivery is deferred. Submission does not fail and
does not discard the batch because of transport state.

Delivery is attempted immediately when the transport is available. Batches
that fail with a retryable transport error become pending batches and are
retried by a later flush.

### Flushing

Flushing delivers pending batches in the order they were accepted. A flush
continues past individual delivery failures caused by retryable transport
errors: a failed batch stays pending and later pending batches are still
attempted. Batches whose delivery fails for reasons the transport contract
does not classify as retryable are not retried; they are retained as failed
pending batches so the caller can inspect and resolve them.

Flushes may be triggered explicitly by the caller and after a restart during
recovery. Concurrent flushes of the same queue record must not duplicate
delivery; an in-flight record is not picked up by a second flush.

### Delivery and conflict resolution

Delivery uses the transport contract's idempotency keys. Each pending batch is
assigned one idempotency key when it first enters the queue and keeps it for
every delivery attempt. This makes redelivery safe: because batches are
independent and carry no mergeable content, the resolution for a repeated
delivery is server-side deduplication by idempotency key, and the resulting
delivery semantics are at-least-once with deduplication. No content-level
merging or last-writer-wins comparison is performed.

The same idempotency key is never reused for different batches, and a batch's
key is never regenerated between attempts. Changing a key would turn a safe
redelivery into a duplicate; that is the conflict this rule prevents.

### Persisted queue state

Pending batches are persisted as queue records using the persistence
contract's durable record encoding. A queue record contains the batch, its
idempotency key, its acceptance order, and its state (pending, in flight, or
failed). Batch content is stored as supplied; the queue does not transform or
interpret batch content.

Queue records are written before submission reports acceptance, so an
accepted batch is never lost to a crash. The queue is the only local state
this specification adds; no separate index, journal, or sidecar state is
introduced.

### Queue migration and compatibility

Queue records carry a schema version and are migrated using the persistence
contract's schema migration mechanism. A queue written by an older version is
upgraded when it is next loaded, before any flush uses it.

Compatibility rules:

- Records written by an older schema version must be readable and upgradable;
  an upgrade must not drop pending batches.
- Unknown fields in a record are preserved when rewriting, not discarded.
- A record that cannot be migrated is quarantined rather than deleted, and
  the remaining queue stays usable.

Downgrade behavior is not guaranteed: a queue written by a newer schema
version may be unreadable by an older implementation. This is the only
compatibility direction this specification promises.

### Recovery

Recovery runs when the queue is next opened after a crash or restart and
operates within the persistence contract's recovery boundaries; `batch-sdk`
does not implement its own recovery mechanism on top of raw storage.

On recovery:

- Records marked in flight revert to pending so they are retried. Idempotency
  keys make that retry safe even if delivery actually completed.
- Pending and failed records are kept with their order and idempotency keys
  unchanged.
- Unreadable or unupgradable records are quarantined, per migration rules.
- After recovery, a flush may be attempted.

Recovery never invents new batches, renumbers accepted order, or changes
idempotency keys.

## Contracts this specification builds on

- [Transport contract](../../../../../../packages/transport-contract/docs/development/specifications/transport/index.md):
  owns request delivery, the retryable transport error classification, and
  idempotency keys. This specification defers to it and does not redefine any
  of those.
- [Persistence contract](../../../../../../packages/persistence-contract/docs/development/specifications/persistence/index.md):
  owns durable record encoding, schema migration, and recovery boundaries.
  This specification uses those mechanisms and does not duplicate them.

Material choices made here and their reasons are recorded in
[decisions.md](decisions.md).
# Offline synchronization requirements

Requirements for the offline synchronization target defined in
[index.md](index.md). None of these outcomes currently exists: the protocol is
not implemented, so every requirement is Not implemented, Unverified, and
undocumented in user or current-behavior documentation.

| ID | Requirement | Implementation | Verification | Documentation | Primary evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| OFF-001 | Submission accepts a batch regardless of transport availability and reports deferral instead of failing or discarding the batch when delivery is not possible. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-002 | A batch that fails with a retryable transport error, per the transport contract's error classification, is retained as a pending batch for a later flush. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-003 | Flushing delivers pending batches in acceptance order and continues past individual retryable delivery failures. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-004 | Delivery failures that the transport contract does not classify as retryable leave the batch as a failed pending batch, retained for caller inspection, and are not retried. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-005 | Each pending batch is assigned exactly one transport-contract idempotency key on first entering the queue, and that key is reused unchanged for every delivery attempt. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-006 | Concurrent flushes do not deliver the same queue record twice; an in-flight record is not picked up by a second flush. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-007 | A batch is durably persisted as a queue record, using the persistence contract's record encoding, before submission reports acceptance. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-008 | Queue records carry a schema version and are migrated through the persistence contract's migration mechanism, without dropping pending batches. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-009 | Unknown fields in a queue record are preserved across migration and rewrite, and a record that cannot be migrated is quarantined while the rest of the queue stays usable. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-010 | On recovery, records marked in flight revert to pending, pending and failed records keep their acceptance order and idempotency keys, and recovery operates within the persistence contract's recovery boundaries. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |
| OFF-011 | A restart followed by a flush delivers previously pending batches at least once, with redelivery made safe by idempotency keys. | Not implemented | Unverified | Pending | — |

# Batch offline synchronization decisions

Material choices made while authoring the
[batch offline synchronization specification](index.md), recorded here as one
file per Task 010.

## DEC-1: Package ownership and location

The specification is owned by `packages/batch-sdk` at
`docs/development/specifications/batch-offline-sync/`.

Alternatives: a root cross-package specification, or a specification inside
one of the contracts.

Reason: the queue protocol is `batch-sdk` behavior, so it belongs with the
package that would implement it. The transport and persistence contracts
already own the shared rules; the specification links them rather than
restating them, and neither contract needs to grow queue-specific text.

## DEC-2: At-least-once delivery with duplicate resolution by idempotency key

Deferred batches are re-delivered until the transport confirms acceptance,
and repeated attempts are made harmless by reusing the transport contract's
idempotency key.

Alternatives: at-most-once delivery, which never repeats an attempt.

Reason: offline synchronization must not lose an accepted batch during a
failure or recovery window. The cost of at-least-once is duplicate delivery
attempts, which the transport contract's idempotency keys already make safe
to repeat and resolve. At-most-once would trade a resolvable failure for an
unresolvable loss.

## DEC-3: FIFO ordering by acceptance

The queue re-delivers batches in the order they were accepted.

Alternatives: priority ordering, parallel flushing, or unspecified ordering.

Reason: acceptance order is the simplest order a caller can predict and
verify, and it needs no additional record fields. Constraints on ordering can
be added later without changing the encoding.

## DEC-4: Non-retryable rejections are retained and surfaced

A deferred batch rejected with a non-retryable transport error stays in the
queue as failed and is surfaced to the caller; the SDK neither retries nor
silently drops it.

Alternatives: dropping the batch and reporting the failure in the submission
result only, or retrying despite the non-retryable classification.

Reason: silently discarding caller data is the worst outcome and retrying a
non-retryable error contradicts the transport contract's classification.
Retaining the failed batch leaves the decision about discarding with the
caller, who owns the data.

## DEC-5: Smallest file set with a single decisions file

The specification consists of one specification page, `requirements.md`, and
this single `decisions.md`.

Alternatives: separate product, technical, and testing-strategy pages, or a
`decisions/` directory with one record per decision.

Reason: the documentation guide's smallest useful structure is sufficient
while the behavior is an unimplemented target; the task explicitly requires
one decisions file and forbids a decisions directory.

## DEC-6: Reuse contract vocabulary, define only new queue terms

The specification reuses the contract terms verbatim — retryable transport
errors, idempotency keys, durable record encoding, schema migration, and
recovery boundaries — and introduces only the terms it must own: deferred
batch, deferred-batch queue, and delivery conflict, each defined at first use.

Alternatives: new terms for contract-owned concepts (for example, a
package-local synonym for idempotency key), or leaving the new terms
undefined.

Reason: a second vocabulary for the same contract concepts would invite drift
between the contracts and this specification, while undefined queue terms
would leave the package-specific behavior ambiguous.
# Batch offline synchronization

Status: approved target, not implemented. This specification describes
intended `batch-sdk` behavior; no part of the protocol exists yet. Requirements
and their states are tracked in [requirements.md](requirements.md).

## Purpose and scope

`batch-sdk` submits batches through the shared
[transport contract](../../../../../transport-contract/docs/development/specifications/transport/index.md).
Today `submit_batch` reports an immediate submission count and gives callers
no way to preserve a batch when the transport cannot deliver it. This
specification defines the package-owned target for offline synchronization:
accepting a batch while delivery is impossible, keeping it durable, and
delivering it later without losing or duplicating it.

The transport contract owns delivery, retryable transport errors, and
idempotency keys. The
[persistence contract](../../../../../persistence-contract/docs/development/specifications/persistence/index.md)
owns durable record encoding, schema migration, and recovery boundaries. This
specification links both contracts and adds the queue protocol on top; it
does not restate or weaken either contract.

## Terms

- **Deferred batch**: a batch the SDK has accepted from the caller but has not
  yet delivered through the transport.
- **Deferred-batch queue**: the durable record of deferred batches, in the
  order they were accepted.
- **Delivery conflict**: a disagreement between the queue's pending state and
  the state the transport reports during re-delivery, such as a batch already
  accepted under its idempotency key or a batch rejected as a duplicate.

## Deferral and delivery

When a caller submits a batch and the transport reports a retryable transport
error, the SDK defers the batch instead of reporting it submitted. The
submission result distinguishes batches that were submitted from batches that
were deferred, so a caller can never mistake a deferred batch for delivered.

Before its first delivery attempt, a deferred batch is assigned an idempotency
key as defined by the transport contract. The same key is reused, unchanged,
for every later delivery attempt, so re-delivery after a failure or reconnect
is safe to repeat.

Delivery is at-least-once: the SDK re-delivers deferred batches until the
transport confirms acceptance. Duplicate delivery attempts are resolved
through the batch's idempotency key, which makes the extra attempts harmless.

## Persisted queue

Deferred batches are recorded in the persistence contract's durable record
encoding, so a deferred batch survives process restarts. The queue preserves
the order in which batches were accepted, and re-delivery follows that order.

A persisted deferred batch carries at least its idempotency key and the
caller's batch payload, which is the minimum needed to re-deliver it and to
resolve delivery conflicts.

## Queue migration and compatibility

Deferred-batch queue records follow the persistence contract's schema
migration behavior. A queue written by an earlier schema version or an
earlier version of `batch-sdk` remains readable and deliverable after an
upgrade, so an application that upgrades with a non-empty queue loses no
batch and gains no duplicate.

## Recovery

After a restart, the SDK recovers the deferred-batch queue within the
persistence contract's recovery boundaries, preserving the recorded order.
Recovered batches are re-delivered once the transport is available again,
using their original idempotency keys.

## Conflict resolution

When re-delivery produces a delivery conflict, the SDK resolves it as follows:

- The transport reports the batch already accepted under its idempotency key:
  the batch is treated as delivered exactly once and removed from the queue.
- The transport rejects the batch with a retryable transport error: the batch
  stays deferred and is attempted again later.
- The transport rejects the batch with a non-retryable error: the batch stays
  in the queue as failed and is surfaced to the caller. It is not retried and
  not silently dropped; the caller decides what happens to it.

## Implementation note

No part of this protocol is implemented. `submit_batch` currently reports only
an immediate submission count, and the package development index describes
this specification as the approved target. See [requirements.md](requirements.md)
for the completion state, and [decisions.md](decisions.md) for the material
choices made while authoring this specification.
# Batch offline synchronization requirements

Specification: [index.md](index.md). Decisions: [decisions.md](decisions.md).

All requirements describe the approved target and currently begin not
implemented and unverified, per Task 010.

| ID | Requirement | Implementation | Verification | Documentation | Primary evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BOS-001 | A batch submitted while the transport reports a retryable transport error is deferred and durably recorded instead of reported as submitted, and the submission result distinguishes submitted from deferred batches. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-002 | Each deferred batch carries an idempotency key assigned before its first delivery attempt and reused unchanged for every later attempt. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-003 | Deferred batches are persisted in the persistence contract's durable record encoding and re-delivered in the order they were accepted. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-004 | Deferred-batch queue records survive a persistence-contract schema migration. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-005 | A queue written by an earlier schema version or an earlier version of `batch-sdk` remains readable and deliverable after an upgrade, with no batch lost and no batch duplicated. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-006 | After a restart, deferred batches are recovered within the persistence contract's recovery boundaries, preserving recorded order, and re-delivered once the transport is available. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-007 | A deferred batch the transport reports as already accepted under its idempotency key is treated as delivered exactly once and removed from the queue. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-008 | A deferred batch rejected with a non-retryable transport error stays in the queue as failed and is surfaced to the caller, neither retried nor silently dropped. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |

# product specification

all clients submit non-empty text messages through a composer. portable
behavior covers message validity, submission, and composer interaction, and
applies identically to every client.

composer interaction requires:

- multiline text input;
- keeping the text input visible while the keyboard is open;
- a send button at the trailing edge of the input row;
- accessibility labels on the text input and send button.

message validity and submission are implemented by existing clients. the
composer interaction requirements above are targets; implementation and
verification are pending. see [requirements](requirements.md).

| composer-001 | clients submit non-empty text. | implemented | automated | documented | existing clients |
| composer-002 | composers accept multiline text input. | pending | pending | pending | — |
| composer-003 | composers keep the text input visible while the keyboard is open. | pending | pending | pending | — |
| composer-004 | composers place the send button at the trailing edge of the input row. | pending | pending | pending | — |
| composer-005 | composers label the text input and send button for assistive technology. | pending | pending | pending | — |

# Batch SDK offline synchronization decisions

Material decisions for the [offline synchronization specification](index.md),
authorized by `tasks/batch-offline-sync.md` (Task 010). Each decision was
taken among credible alternatives; none is implemented yet.

## D-1 At-least-once delivery with idempotency-key deduplication

**Decision.** A pending batch is resubmitted until its delivery is confirmed;
re-delivery of an already-delivered batch is acceptable and identified by its
idempotency key.

**Alternatives.** At-most-once delivery (remove a record on send attempt);
exactly-once delivery.

**Reason.** Removing a record on send attempt loses the batch whenever the
outcome is unknown after an interruption. Exactly-once delivery needs
transactional outcome recording the transport contract does not provide. The
transport contract already provides idempotency keys, so duplicates are
collapsible without additional protocol state.

## D-2 Deferral reuses the transport contract's error classification

**Decision.** A batch is deferred only when delivery fails with a retryable
transport error; non-retryable failures are surfaced to the caller and not
queued.

**Alternatives.** Defer every failed submission; define an SDK-specific
deferral classification.

**Reason.** Queueing non-retryable failures creates records that can never be
delivered and permanently block reconciliation work. A second classification
would duplicate a boundary the transport contract already owns and could
diverge from it.

## D-3 Conflicts are surfaced, never silently resolved

**Decision.** Differing content under a recorded idempotency key is surfaced
as a conflict to the caller, and the recorded pending batch is kept
unchanged.

**Alternatives.** Last-writer-wins on key collision; drop the newer or older
record automatically.

**Reason.** Pending batches are durable records of caller data. Silent
overwrite or drop is indistinguishable from data loss for the losing side, and
no user need for automatic resolution was identified.

## D-4 Idempotency keys are immutable from deferral time

**Decision.** The key assigned at deferral time is stable across retries,
restarts, and queue migration.

**Alternatives.** Generate a fresh key per retry or per process start.

**Reason.** Regenerating keys defeats duplicate suppression and could deliver
the same batch as distinct batches after an interruption.

## D-5 Queue state follows the persistence contract

**Decision.** Pending batches are stored in the persistence contract's record
encoding and migrated by its schema migration; the SDK defines no private
queue format or migration path.

**Alternatives.** An SDK-private queue file with its own versioning.

**Reason.** A parallel format would create a second compatibility surface to
keep aligned with the same durability, migration, and recovery guarantees the
persistence contract already maintains.

## D-6 Records leave the queue only on confirmed delivery

**Decision.** A pending record is removed only when its delivery outcome has
been durably recorded as delivered.

**Alternatives.** Remove optimistically before or during the send attempt.

**Reason.** Optimistic removal makes an interruption indistinguishable from
success and silently loses the batch; retention until confirmation is what
makes D-1 safe.

## D-7 No cross-batch ordering guarantee

**Decision.** Reconciliation may submit pending batches in any order;
cross-batch delivery order is not guaranteed, including after recovery.

**Alternatives.** Strict first-in-first-out ordering across restarts.

**Reason.** Batches are independent submissions; strict global ordering would
require sequencing and head-of-line blocking across restarts for no identified
consumer need. Consumers needing order must encode it in batch content.

## D-8 Deferral is reported in the submission result

**Decision.** The submission result distinguishes delivered batches from
deferred batches instead of raising an offline failure or blocking until
connectivity returns.

**Alternatives.** Raise an offline error and require each caller to queue
batches; block the call until delivery is possible.

**Reason.** Blocking ties callers to connectivity they may not have; pushing
queueing to callers would reimplement durability per caller and lose the
shared recovery behavior. A reported deferral keeps the call non-blocking
while making the queue observable.
# Batch SDK offline synchronization

This specification defines the offline synchronization behavior for the batch
SDK: deferring batch submissions that cannot be delivered, queueing them
durably, resubmitting them after connectivity returns, and resolving
conflicts and interruptions without losing or silently replacing a recorded
batch.

**Implementation note.** This specification leads implementation. The current
implementation performs online submission only
(`packages/batch-sdk/src/batch.py`); none of the offline behavior below is
implemented. [requirements.md](requirements.md) tracks the state of each
requirement.

## Scope

In scope:

- deferral of batch submissions when delivery cannot be completed;
- a durable pending queue for deferred batches;
- resubmission of pending batches when delivery becomes possible again;
- conflict resolution for repeated or differing deliveries;
- pending-queue schema migration and compatibility across schema versions;
- recovery of the pending queue after an interruption.

Out of scope:

- transport error classification, retry timing, and idempotency-key format,
  which the transport contract owns;
- durable record encoding mechanics, schema migration mechanics, and recovery
  mechanics, which the persistence contract owns;
- batch content schemas and what consumers do with delivered batches.

## Shared contracts

The offline protocol is defined on top of two existing contracts and does not
restate or replace either:

- [Transport contract](../../../../../transport-contract/docs/development/specifications/transport/index.md):
  request delivery, retryable transport errors, and idempotency keys. This
  protocol consumes that error classification and key mechanism; it defines no
  retry policy or key format of its own.
- [Persistence contract](../../../../../persistence-contract/docs/development/specifications/persistence/index.md):
  durable record encoding, schema migration, and recovery boundaries. The
  pending queue is encoded, migrated, and recovered within those boundaries.

## Terms

- **Deferral**: recording a batch for later delivery instead of reporting a
  failed submission when delivery cannot be completed now.
- **Pending batch**: a batch recorded durably that has not been confirmed as
  delivered.
- **Pending queue**: the durable set of pending batches.
- **Idempotency key**: the key defined by the transport contract that
  identifies a batch across delivery attempts.
- **Reconciliation**: a pass that submits pending batches.
- **Confirmed**: a delivery outcome the SDK has durably recorded as delivered.
- **Conflict**: delivery activity for a recorded idempotency key whose content
  differs from the recorded batch.

## Submission and deferral

- Submission attempts go through the shared transport contract.
- When delivery fails with a retryable transport error, the batch is deferred:
  it is recorded durably as a pending batch, and the submission result reports
  it as deferred rather than submitted.
- When delivery fails with an error the transport contract classifies as
  non-retryable, the failure is surfaced to the caller and the batch is not
  deferred.
- A deferred batch is recorded together with its idempotency key, assigned
  once at deferral time.

## Delivery semantics

- Delivery is at-least-once: a pending batch is resubmitted until its delivery
  is confirmed. An interruption between a delivery attempt and recording its
  outcome can re-deliver an already-delivered batch; the idempotency key lets
  the receiving side collapse such duplicates.
- A pending batch leaves the queue only when its delivery is confirmed.
  Records are not removed on a send attempt, because the outcome would then be
  unknown.
- Batches are independent; cross-batch delivery order is not guaranteed (see
  [decisions.md](decisions.md)).

## Conflict resolution

- Delivery under a recorded idempotency key always carries the recorded batch
  content; a key is never reused for different content.
- If submission activity presents a recorded idempotency key with different
  content, or the transport reports a key as delivered with different content
  than recorded, the SDK surfaces a conflict to the caller and keeps the
  recorded pending batch unchanged. Conflicts are never silently overwritten
  or dropped.

## Persisted queue, migration, and compatibility

- Each pending batch is one durable record using the persistence contract's
  record encoding. The record carries the batch content, its idempotency key,
  the queue schema version, and its deferral state.
- Opening a pending queue written by an older supported schema version
  migrates it through the persistence contract's schema migration. Migration
  preserves recorded batch content and idempotency keys, so the delivery
  semantics of existing records do not change across migration.
- Which schema versions remain supported is bounded by the migration the
  persistence contract supports; this specification adds no separate queue
  format or compatibility mechanism.

## Recovery

- After an interruption, the pending queue is recovered at start-up within the
  persistence contract's recovery boundaries.
- Records not confirmed as delivered after recovery are resubmitted under
  their recorded idempotency keys during reconciliation.
- Records confirmed as delivered before the interruption are not resubmitted.

## Non-guarantees

- Cross-batch delivery order is not guaranteed, including after recovery.
- Duplicate suppression relies on idempotency keys; batches submitted without
  a recorded key are outside the offline protocol.
# Batch SDK offline synchronization requirements

All requirements below describe target behavior authorized by
`tasks/batch-offline-sync.md` (Task 010). The offline synchronization protocol
is not implemented; no requirement is verified. States use the Crystal Lattice
vocabulary: implementation `Not started`, verification `Unverified`,
documentation `Pending`.

| ID | Requirement | Implementation | Verification | Documentation | Primary evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BOS-001 | A submission attempt reports delivered batches separately from deferred batches in its result. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-002 | A batch whose delivery fails with a retryable transport error is durably deferred; it is neither lost nor reported as submitted. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-003 | A deferred batch's idempotency key is assigned at deferral time and stays stable across retries, restarts, and queue migration. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-004 | A deferred batch is resubmitted until its delivery is confirmed; re-delivery under the same idempotency key is treated as delivered. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-005 | Delivery under a recorded idempotency key always carries the same batch content; differing content for a recorded key is surfaced as a conflict and is neither silently overwritten nor dropped. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-006 | Deferred batches are persisted as durable records using the persistence contract's record encoding. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |
| BOS-007 | A pending queue written by an older supported schema version is migrated through the persistence contract's schema migration without changing the delivery semantics of existing records. | Not started | Unverified | Pending | — |

# Publishing events

Call `publish(event)` to publish an event. It returns the published status
together with the event payload:

```python
publish({"type": "created"})
# {"status": "published", "event": {"type": "created"}}
```

## Retry behavior

Transient delivery failures are classified by a retry state machine:

- `retry_state(attempt, max_attempts=3)` returns `"retrying"` while the
  attempt count is below the configured limit.
- An attempt at or beyond the limit returns `"failed"`. The default limit
  is 3 attempts.

```python
retry_state(1)  # "retrying"
retry_state(3)  # "failed"
```

# mobile composer ux refinement

this specification defines the mobile presentation and interaction refinement
for the composer in the example app. it supplements the
[portable composer contract](../../../../../../packages/conversation-contract/docs/development/specifications/composer/index.md);
the portable contract remains authoritative for message validity and

composer or surrounding content for the keyboard. the send control is placed

# Batch offline synchronization decisions

These decisions record the material Stage A choices for the target protocol.
They do not indicate that the protocol has been implemented.

## D-001: Keep the synchronization semantics with the batch SDK

The batch SDK specification defines how a batch becomes a durable local
submission, how it is replayed, and how its conflicts are represented. The
transport and persistence contracts remain the sources of truth for their
respective delivery and durable-record mechanics. This keeps the package
specific lifecycle together without copying or altering either shared
contract.

## D-002: Durable intent precedes queued acceptance

A batch is an offline synchronization intent, not a remote success. The SDK
must durably preserve the payload and stable submission identity before
reporting queued acceptance. This prevents a process failure immediately after
acceptance from turning into an untraceable submission.

## D-003: Replay is at-least-once at the SDK boundary, with stable identity

Delivery may be attempted more than once because a connection or process can
fail after the remote side receives a request. The SDK therefore does not
claim exactly-once execution by itself. It reuses one idempotency key for all
attempts of one queue record and relies on the transport contract's
idempotency behavior to reconcile duplicate delivery.

## D-004: Conflicts are preserved, not automatically merged

Different payloads must not overwrite or merge under one submission identity.
An identity or acknowledgement conflict is kept recoverable and excluded from
automatic delivery until explicit reconciliation is possible. This avoids
turning uncertain delivery into silent data loss or an untraceable mutation.

## D-005: Queue migration is conservative

Supported older queue records may be migrated, but the source remains
recoverable until the migrated representation is durable. Unsupported newer
records and failed migrations are not guessed at, rewritten, or delivered
automatically. This follows the persistence contract's emphasis on schema
migration and recovery boundaries.

## D-006: Completion is a durable lifecycle transition

A queue record is not removed from the pending set merely because a request
was sent. It becomes complete only after a success acknowledgement and the
corresponding state transition are durable. Recovery can therefore distinguish
completed records from interrupted or unresolved attempts.

# Batch offline synchronization

Status: target specification; not implemented.

## Purpose and scope

This specification defines the target behavior for accepting batch submissions
when delivery is unavailable and synchronizing them when delivery becomes
available. It covers the boundary between the batch SDK, the shared transport
contract, and durable queued state.

The current implementation is online-only: `submit_batch(items)` returns a
count and does not create a transport request or persisted record. This page
describes intended behavior for a future implementation and must not be read
as a description of currently supported SDK behavior.

The specification covers:

- durable acceptance of a batch submission before it is acknowledged as queued;
- delivery and replay through the transport contract;
- stable identity and idempotency across retries and process restarts;
- persisted queue schema evolution and migration;
- conflict handling and recovery after failures or interruption; and
- compatibility between queued records and the shared contracts.

It does not define the wire format of transport requests, the transport
library's retry policy, or the persistence library's encoding and migration
mechanisms. Those remain defined by the
[transport contract](../../../../../transport-contract/docs/development/specifications/transport/index.md)
and [persistence contract](../../../../../persistence-contract/docs/development/specifications/persistence/index.md).

## Terms

- A **queued batch** is a locally accepted submission whose delivery has not
  reached a durable successful terminal state.
- A **queue record** is the durable representation of one queued batch,
  including the batch payload, stable submission identity, schema version, and
  lifecycle state.
- A **replay** is another delivery attempt for the same queue record. A replay
  keeps the record's submission identity and idempotency key.
- A **conflict** occurs when records with the same submission identity do not
  describe the same batch, or when an acknowledgement cannot be reconciled
  with the queue record that produced it.

## Required lifecycle

### Accept

The SDK must write a queue record durably before reporting that a batch has
been accepted for offline synchronization. The record must preserve the
submitted payload and a stable submission identity. A process or connectivity
failure before that durable boundary must not be reported as successful
offline acceptance.

The queue record is an intent to submit; it is not evidence that the remote
service has accepted the batch.

### Deliver

When delivery is available, the SDK must submit the queued batch through the
transport contract. Each attempt for a queue record must use the record's
stable idempotency key. Retryable transport errors leave the record eligible
for replay. A successful acknowledgement moves the record to a durable
completed state.

The SDK must not create a new logical submission merely because an attempt is
retried, the process restarts, or the connection changes from offline to
online.

### Complete and retain history

Completion must be durable before the SDK treats a queue record as no longer
pending. A completed record must not be replayed as a new submission during
normal recovery. Retention and deletion of completed records remain subject to
the persistence contract and any later package policy; deletion must not be
used to hide an unresolved delivery or migration failure.

### Recover

Recovery must inspect durable queue state after startup or interruption:

- an interrupted in-flight attempt is returned to a replayable state;
- a retryable transport failure remains pending;
- a non-retryable or otherwise unresolved failure remains represented with
  enough information to diagnose and explicitly recover it; and
- an already completed record is not submitted again.

The SDK must not silently discard a record when delivery, acknowledgement
processing, or recovery fails.

## Conflict resolution

Submission identity and idempotency key are stable properties of a queue
record, not properties regenerated for each attempt. Replaying the same
record with the same payload is the normal duplicate-delivery case and is
resolved through the transport contract's idempotency behavior.

The SDK must not merge or overwrite two different payloads that claim the
same submission identity. Such a record is a conflict and must remain
recoverable and distinguishable from successful completion. The conflicting
record must be quarantined or otherwise prevented from automatic delivery
until it can be resolved without changing the identity of an already-issued
submission.

An acknowledgement that cannot be associated with the originating submission
is also a conflict. Recovery must preserve the queue record and the
acknowledgement information needed for explicit reconciliation; it must not
mark the batch completed solely because an unrelated acknowledgement exists.

## Persisted queue migration

Queue records are versioned according to the persistence contract. A reader
must recognize the record versions supported by the SDK and migrate an older
supported version before delivery. Migration must preserve the batch payload,
submission identity, idempotency key, and lifecycle meaning.

Migration must have a recoverable boundary. The original record remains
recoverable until the migrated record is durably written and selected for
use. A record written by a newer, unsupported schema version must not be
silently rewritten or interpreted as a current record. Migration failure
leaves the record visible as unresolved and prevents automatic delivery of an
untrusted representation.

The SDK's queue semantics therefore depend on, but do not replace, the
persistence contract's durable encoding, schema migration, and recovery
boundaries.

## Compatibility

The batch SDK must remain compatible with the transport contract by:

- using its request-delivery boundary for online delivery and replay;
- classifying transport outcomes according to the contract's retryable
  transport errors; and
- retaining one idempotency key across every attempt for one queue record.

It must remain compatible with the persistence contract by:

- treating queue records as durable records rather than process-local state;
- using the contract's encoding and schema-version rules for persisted data;
  and
- respecting the contract's recovery boundary when a write, migration, or
  read is interrupted.

The package specification adds queue lifecycle, conflict, and replay semantics
at this boundary. It does not redefine either shared contract or assume that
transport delivery alone provides durable local state.

## Non-goals

This specification does not define:

- a transport wire schema or provider-specific request format;
- a particular storage engine or serialization library;
- an exactly-once guarantee beyond the idempotency behavior available from the
  transport contract;
- automatic merging of different batch payloads; or
- implementation changes to `submit_batch` or any other source file.

## Implementation status

This is the Stage A target specification. The protocol is not implemented,
verified, or available as current SDK behavior. See the
[requirements](requirements.md) for the detailed status record and
[decisions](decisions.md) for the material choices that constrain a future
implementation.

# Batch offline synchronization requirements

These requirements describe the Stage A target. They intentionally begin as
not implemented and unverified because this stage documents the protocol
without implementing it.

| ID | Requirement | Implementation | Verification | Documentation | Primary evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BATCH-OFFLINE-001 | A batch accepted for offline synchronization is durably represented before the SDK reports queued acceptance, with its payload and stable submission identity preserved. | Not implemented | Unverified | Documented | [Accept](index.md#accept) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-002 | Delivery and replay use the shared transport contract, including its retryable-error classification and idempotency-key behavior. | Not implemented | Unverified | Documented | [Deliver](index.md#deliver) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-003 | Every replay of one queued batch retains the same submission identity and idempotency key, and successful completion is durable before the record leaves the pending set. | Not implemented | Unverified | Documented | [Deliver](index.md#deliver), [Complete and retain history](index.md#complete-and-retain-history) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-004 | Startup and interruption recovery preserve unresolved records, make interrupted attempts replayable, and do not replay records already durably completed. | Not implemented | Unverified | Documented | [Recover](index.md#recover) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-005 | Conflicting payloads or unmatchable acknowledgements are not silently merged, overwritten, or marked successful; they remain distinguishable and recoverable. | Not implemented | Unverified | Documented | [Conflict resolution](index.md#conflict-resolution) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-006 | Supported older queue-record versions can be migrated without changing payload, identity, idempotency, or lifecycle meaning, while unsupported or failed migrations remain recoverable and are not auto-delivered. | Not implemented | Unverified | Documented | [Persisted queue migration](index.md#persisted-queue-migration) |
| BATCH-OFFLINE-007 | Queue behavior respects the transport and persistence contracts without redefining their request, error, encoding, migration, or recovery mechanisms. | Not implemented | Unverified | Documented | [Compatibility](index.md#compatibility) |

## Shared evidence and status

The package development index links this specification and the two shared
contracts. No implementation, automated verification, or runtime evidence
exists for these requirements in Stage A. The current `submit_batch(items)`
implementation remains online-only and is not evidence for any requirement
above.

# Batch SDK development

The batch SDK currently exposes an online-only `submit_batch(items)` function.
Its implementation returns the number of supplied items and does not yet
persist, deliver, retry, or recover batches.

The target behavior for offline synchronization is documented in the
[offline synchronization specification](specifications/offline-synchronization/index.md).
That specification is not implemented. Its progress and evidence are tracked
in the [requirements](specifications/offline-synchronization/requirements.md),
and material design choices are recorded in
[decisions](specifications/offline-synchronization/decisions.md).

The target depends on the shared [transport contract](../../../transport-contract/docs/development/specifications/transport/index.md)
for request delivery, retryable transport errors, and idempotency keys, and on
the [persistence contract](../../../persistence-contract/docs/development/specifications/persistence/index.md)
for durable encoding, schema migration, and recovery boundaries. The batch
specification defines how those concerns apply to a queued batch; it does not
restate either contract.

# Publishing events

Call `publish(event)` to return a published event result:

```python
publish({"type": "created"})
# {"status": "published", "event": {"type": "created"}}
```

`publish()` currently reports the event as published. It does not perform
delivery attempts or automatically retry a failed delivery.

To determine the retry state for an attempt, call `retry_state(attempt,
max_attempts=3)`. It returns `"retrying"` while `attempt` is below
`max_attempts`, and `"failed"` once `attempt` reaches or exceeds that limit.
The helper reports the state; it does not perform the retry or persist the
event.

owner: `mobile/example-app`

this specification refines the
[portable composer contract](../../../../../../packages/conversation-contract/docs/development/specifications/composer/index.md)
for the mobile composer. the portable contract remains authoritative for
message validity and submission; this refinement defines mobile interaction,
layout, and accessibility behavior only.

- [product specification](product-spec.md)
- [requirements](requirements.md)

the refinement is a target specification. its ui implementation has not

# product specification

the mobile composer is a multiline input for composing a message before it is
submitted through the
[portable composer contract](../../../../../../packages/conversation-contract/docs/development/specifications/composer/index.md).
line breaks entered by the user remain part of the draft until submission.
the mobile refinement does not redefine the portable contract's message
validity or submission behavior.

## keyboard avoidance

when the software keyboard is visible, the composer layout keeps both the
multiline input and the send button visible and usable. the keyboard must not
cover either control.

## send-button placement

the send button is part of the composer action area, placed at the trailing
edge of the composer and aligned with the lower edge of the multiline input.
it remains associated with the input while the software keyboard is visible.

## accessibility labels

the multiline input exposes the accessible label `message`. the send button
exposes the accessible label `send message`. these labels identify the
controls to assistive technologies independently of their visual presentation.
# requirements

the portable message-validity and submission requirement remains defined by the
